Subject: Hosted evaluation: deployment mode clarifications + access checklist

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the clear walkthrough of the patient routing use case. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the open items so we can keep momentum on the eval and make a recommendation for Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private. Short version up-front: based on the traffic profile you shared and the PHI requirements, Hosted is likely suitable for an initial pilot if we enable VPC peering and contractually lock data residency; Dedicated or Private would be recommended if you need on-prem processing or strict tenant isolation for full production.

Open questions for you (short bullets so procurement/IT can forward):
- Expected RPS and burst pattern (sample per-hour over peak day) — I attached a simple traffic matrix you can fill.
- Are you able to accept a hosted SaaS endpoint with VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest? Or is on-prem/on-airgap required?
- Compliance evidence we should prepare up front (SOC 2 attestation, retention/MDM controls, optional pen-test report).

Proposed next steps:
1) You complete the attached traffic matrix and return by EOD Tue 9/14.
2) We set a 30-min technical sync w/ Sean (solutions engineer) to map endpoints, expected rate caps, and token scopes — propose Wed 9/15 or Thu 9/16.
3) Redwood supplies a short hosted-onramp ops checklist + sandbox credentials (48h) for an evaluation pass.

Attachments: luma_traffic_matrix.csv, mutual_action_plan_v1.docx

Thanks — I’ll loop Aditya on recommendations once we get the traffic matrix back.

—

Thanks Erin — appreciate the fast turnaround and the filled matrix. I reviewed the numbers and sketched a recommended evaluation plan below (keeping the pilot on Hosted but configuring controls you asked about).

Recommended pilot configuration (Hosted-first):
- Tier: Hosted API trial with dedicated tenant (logical isolation) + VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. This satisfies most procurement/security asks while giving you quick time-to-value.
- Endpoints: 2 endpoints to start — /v1/generate-chat (for routing/responses) and /v1/embeddings (for similarity search). We’ll provide a sandbox hostname in the form sandbox-useast.redwood.api/lumahealth.
- Rate caps: Baseline per-endpoint cap set to 100 RPS with burst capacity to 200 RPS for 120s windows. For the reported peak (120 RPS), we recommend a canary where initial production traffic is limited to 80% of burst for 48h while we monitor token latencies.
- KV/prefix caching: Enable prefix caching for repeated prompts to lower cost; we’ll share batching guidance to keep 95th percentile latency under 400ms for chat generation.

Operational checklist for the pilot (what Redwood will deliver within 48–72h after sign-off):
- Sandbox credentials + short-lived API keys.
- Rateplan and token cost estimate (attached: recommended_rateplan.xlsx).
- SOC 2 Type II summary and pen-test abstract.
- Mutual action plan with milestones and a short rollback strategy.

If LumaHealth confirms Hosted with VPC + KMS, we’ll prepare an MSA addendum and an Access Request Form for your cloud team to configure peering. If procurement needs a pricing anchor for the pilot, see tab 2 of the attached rateplan.

Action items:
- Erin: confirm Wed 9/15 11:00am ET for tech sync (Sean to lead).
- Vanessa: I’ll draft the pilot addendum and drop the sandbox creds once we have a signed acceptance email.

—
